summary: This lecture covers the ninth chapter from Al-Wajeez regarding the instances in which it is preferred (mustahabb) for a person to perform wudu (ritual ablution). The instructor reviews nine instances where wudu is recommended: dhikr (remembrance of Allah), eating food cooked on open flame, consumption during janabah (ritual impurity), before every session of salat (prayer), after breaking wudu, after vomiting, before listening to Quran, at the start of bathing, and after carrying or bathing a deceased body (janazah). The lecture emphasizes the distinction between obligatory instances of wudu (salat, touching the Quran, tawaf) and preferred instances. For the final instance regarding janazah, the instructor harmonizes two seemingly contradictory hadith narrations to conclude that making wudu after carrying a body and ghusl after bathing one are preferred rather than obligatory practices.
